newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bills rally while kiwi dlr closes unchanged.
newsitem.headline: NZ bills rally while kiwi dlr closes unchanged.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous trading day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 91.97 (PREV 91.82) 90-DAYS 8.26 (PREV 8.41)
OVERNIGHT CASH 8.10 PCT (PREV 8.30) US 5-YR 6.10 (PREV 6.15)
RBNZ MCI NZ/MCI 709.64 (PREV 709.02) Reuters NZ MCI-115 vs-114
New Zealand bank bill yields fell 15 basis points on Friday while the New Zealand dollar closed unchanged after trading in a wide band.
The bills were helped by the Trade-Weighted Index which gained 20 points to 64.13 but dealers said there was outright buying in the bill market.
Sentiment was bullish and traders were not put off by stronger that expected June quarter retail sales data.
"The market just wants to be bullish at the moment so they are just ignoring numbers like that," said a Wellington bank chief dealer.
He said the market's decision to ignore the Reserve Bank was becoming a concern.
The market showed little fear about the RB despite the Monetary Conditions Index closing 115 basis points easier than the desired level for the September quarter.
Dealers now rate the bank's comfort zone around 100-110 points below 825 on the MCI.
Bill bill futures were keenly sought at 91.85. They ended at 91.97 on volume of 3354.
One dealer said the retail sales data was ignored and the focus is next Friday's Labour Cost index and business confidence surveys the following week.
There was light activity in the bond market with most action in the short bonds which were feeding off the bill market.
The 02/00 bonds closed 12 basis points lower at 7.24 percent and the 11/06 bonds closed 10 points lower at 6.99 percent.
The kiwi dollar finished at US$0.6412/19 after trading a 0.6388-0.6416 range.
It was sold a tad on the retail sales data but came back well bid in the afternoon. Dealers said the market was slightly short and a firming Australian dollar had pulled it up with it.
"It depends on what the the aussie does but it's pretty firm at the moment so I think we'll stay up," said a dealer.
He predicts it will remain in a 0.6380-0.6430 range over the weekend
